questions.question: When loading or unloading explosive materials, what should you do?

options.text: Use sharp tools to open packages.

questions.explanation: Always turn off your engine before loading or unloading explosives. Never drop, throw, or roll packages with explosives.

questions.question: What shape are hazardous materials warning placards?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: After an accident with hazardous materials, which is NOT your job as the driver?

options.text: Keep people away from the scene.
Try to put out a hazardous materials fire yourself.
Tell emergency workers about the hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to put out a hazardous materials fire yourself.
questions.explanation: Your job is to keep people away, limit the spread of materials if safe, and tell emergency workers about the dangers. Do not try to fight a hazardous materials fire yourself unless you have training and protective equipment.

questions.question: What is a Class 7 hazardous material?
questions.explanation: Radioactive materials are Class 7 hazardous materials.

questions.question: When loading corrosive materials, what should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: Load breakable containers of corrosive liquid one at a time by hand. Keep them upright. Do not drop or roll the containers.

questions.question: What shape are hazardous materials placards on vehicles?
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs on all four sides. These signs are called placards.

questions.question: Where must hazardous materials placards be placed?

options.text: On the outside of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the outside of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed on the front, rear, and both sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: What do you need to know to choose the correct placards?

options.text: The hazard class of the materials.
The types of containers holding the materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazard class of the materials.
questions.explanation: You must know the hazard class of the materials, the amount being shipped, and the total weight of all hazardous materials in the vehicle.

questions.question: Before opening trailer doors during a truck fire, what should you do?

options.text: Check if the doors are hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check if the doors are hot.
questions.explanation: Feel the doors to check if they are hot before opening them. If the doors are hot, there may be a cargo fire. Keep the doors closed if there is a cargo fire.

questions.question: What is required when transporting explosives?

options.text: You must have a written route plan.
You should take the shortest possible route.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must have a written route plan.
questions.explanation: You must follow a written route plan when transporting certain explosives. Avoid populated areas, crowds, tunnels, narrow streets, and alleys. Check for any route restrictions.

questions.question: If corrosive materials leak in the trailer, how should the trailer be cleaned?
questions.explanation: Any part of a vehicle exposed to corrosive material must be washed thoroughly with water.

questions.question: What must you do when approaching a railroad crossing while carrying chlorine?

options.text: You must stop before crossing the tracks.
You must slow down before crossing the tracks.
You may cross if no warning lights are flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop before crossing the tracks.
questions.explanation: When carrying any amount of chlorine, always stop at a railroad crossing. Stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track, no matter if a train is present or not.

questions.question: If a vehicle carrying Class 1 explosives crashes, what should the driver do?

options.text: Not warn others of the danger.
Keep the explosives in the vehicle until after separating it from the other vehicle.
Remove the explosives from the vehicle before separating it from the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove the explosives from the vehicle before separating it from the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle carrying Class 1 explosives crashes, warn others, keep people away, and do not allow smoking or open fires. Remove all explosives and place them at least 200 feet away from the vehicles and any buildings.

questions.question: What does it mean if the third column of the Hazardous Materials Table says "Forbidden"?

options.text: The substance can only be transported by air.
The substance can only be transported at night.
The substance must have a security guard.

questions.explanation: The third column of the Hazardous Materials Table shows hazard classes. Never transport any material marked "Forbidden."

questions.question: What must shipping papers for hazardous materials include?

options.text: How the materials will be used.

questions.explanation: Shippers must include an emergency response telephone number on hazardous materials shipping papers.

questions.question: How far must a person stay from a vehicle carrying Class 3 or Division 2.1 materials before smoking?
questions.explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a vehicle marked for Class 3 or Division 2.1 hazardous materials.

questions.question: If shipping papers say "Inhalation Hazard," when must you use an inhalation hazard placard?

options.text: Only if carrying more than 100 pounds of the material.
For any amount of the material being transported.
Only if air masks are provided to handlers.

questions.correctAnswerText: For any amount of the material being transported.
questions.explanation: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on shipping papers, display the proper inhalation hazard placard along with other required placards. This applies to any amount of material.

questions.question: When transporting explosives, where may you leave your vehicle unattended?
questions.explanation: You may only leave your vehicle unattended in a safe haven. A safe haven is an approved location for parking unattended vehicles loaded with explosives.

questions.question: When transporting hazardous materials, where must placards be placed?

options.text: On all four sides of the vehicle.
Only by Class A licensed drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all four sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: Where must a hazardous material's ID number appear?

options.text: On a sticker near the shipping container.

questions.explanation: A material's ID number must appear on its shipping paper and packaging. It must also appear on cargo tanks and other bulk containers.

questions.question: If cargo with hazardous materials is leaking, the driver should:

options.text: Drive to find a phone and alert emergency personnel
Drive to a hazardous materials cleanup facility
Park the vehicle and contact emergency personnel

questions.correctAnswerText: Park the vehicle and contact emergency personnel
questions.explanation: When hazardous materials leak, stop driving immediately. Continuing to drive spreads contamination over a larger area. Instead, park the vehicle, secure the area, stay with the vehicle, and get help.

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 materials should not be placed in a trailer with:
questions.explanation: Do not use cargo heaters when transporting Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gases), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials.

questions.question: If a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials:

options.text: The hazardous materials must be listed first
The hazardous materials must be written in larger text
The hazardous materials must be written in red ink

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazardous materials must be listed first
questions.explanation: On shipping papers, hazardous materials must be listed before non-hazardous materials.

questions.question: Before opening trailer doors during a fire, what should you do?

options.text: Feel the doors to check if they are hot
Have someone else open the doors

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel the doors to check if they are hot
questions.explanation: During a truck fire, feel the doors before opening them. Hot doors mean there may be a cargo fire inside. Keep the doors closed because opening them lets in oxygen and makes the fire worse.

questions.question: If you notice a cargo leak, you can identify the leaking cargo by:
questions.explanation: Use shipping papers, labels, or package locations to identify leaking materials. Never touch leaking hazardous materials.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, liquid discharge valves should be:
questions.explanation: Keep liquid discharge valves open during loading and unloading. Keep them closed at all other times.

questions.question: The identification numbers for chemicals can be found in:
questions.explanation: The DOT Emergency Response Guide (ERG) contains information about hazardous chemicals. It is indexed by shipping names and identification numbers.

questions.question: When loading containers of hazardous materials, you should not use:
questions.explanation: Protect containers of hazardous materials. Never use hooks or other equipment that could damage containers or packaging.

questions.question: If cargo is leaking, you should:

options.text: Touch the leaking material to identify it
Use shipping papers and labels to identify the leaking cargo
Assume all the cargo is leaking
Spray the leaking containers with water

questions.correctAnswerText: Use shipping papers and labels to identify the leaking cargo
questions.explanation: When you find a leak in hazardous materials, identify the materials using shipping papers, labels, or package location. Never touch the leaking material.

questions.question: When transporting chlorine, what must be kept in the vehicle?
questions.explanation: When transporting chlorine in cargo tanks, keep an approved gas mask and an emergency kit in the vehicle.
